answer: A stake-weighted reputation graph makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent identity must lock a bond, like an onyx token, before it can trade, and its vertex in the trust graph only gains weight from real completed work. Fake identities appear as a thin nebula of disconnected nodes with no history, so peers discount them. Creating thousands of convincing fake histories costs more than the fraud earns, because reputation cannot be copied, only earned over time.
